title: Why rigid types can hinder changing deployed code
why: Real-world cost is changing deployed code, not writing it; types catch breakage from changes but overly rigid types block common, needed changes.

title: How IRS contractor-vs-employee tests really work
why: Control over means and manner, not results, makes a worker an employee; IRS applies 20 factors in a facts-and-circumstances test easily tipped either way.

title: Which hiring methods actually predict job performance
why: Points to Schmidt and Hunter's meta-analysis of 85 years of selection research as the evidence base for interviews, tests and resume screening.

title: Why Linux overtook Solaris technically and commercially
why: Linux won on performance, observability, drivers and contributor count; ecosystem, staff skills and TCO outweigh a once-superior incumbent.

title: Why one engineer quit building software
why: Opinion about complexity and hiring culture; personal disillusion with software practice, without a concrete technique to learn.

title: Glacier retrieval fees can dwarf storage costs
why: Glacier prices retrieval by peak hourly request rate, so one large restore can cost hundreds of times the monthly storage fee.

title: Self-employment criteria versus marketplace models
why: Argues the French ruling's self-employment criteria fit marketplaces poorly; mostly legal-policy opinion with a loose analogy.

title: Defense of Wolfram's research institute
why: Argues for Wolfram's work and against critics; advocacy rather than an explanation a reader could learn from.

title: Python's limits in large codebases
why: Strong opinion on Python's scale problems; typing and GIL points are gestured at without a worked explanation.

title: Economic critique of corporate headcount norms
why: Argues taxing the wealthy should fund baseline benefits instead of shaming labor-intensive employers; policy opinion.

title: Clarifying a 2007 commenter's YC criticism
why: Moderator defends a commenter's criticism of Dropbox; social context and hindsight, not technical knowledge.

title: Why permanent unique usernames are a bad idea
why: Opinion that permanent unique usernames fail at scale and create impersonation problems; argument without a concrete technique.

title: Anecdotes on SAP's entrenchment and UX
why: Personal experience from public accounting: SAP is deeply entrenched and hard to replace; opinion-led, with little concrete explanation.

title: Argument for letting covid become endemic
why: Policy opinion about vaccination and infection; not technical learning.

title: Compilation of Musk's autonomy predictions
why: Chronology of missed self-driving predictions; a critique of claims rather than an explanation of how systems work.

title: Personal take on family instability
why: Social commentary and personal family story; opinion without a technical or transferable lesson.

title: Why one engineer skips a personal site
why: Personal reasons against personal websites; opinion about self-presentation and employer scrutiny.

title: Skepticism about WeWork's valuation
why: Opinion about startup valuations and founder motives; speculation without a verifiable mechanism.

title: Fair use is an exception to copyright, not a license
why: A license grants permission; fair use is an independent exception, so copying can be lawful without a license, as Google Books showed.

title: Caution about public accusations
why: Social and legal commentary on misconduct accusations; not technical and not a learning resource.

title: Writing every day to finish a book
why: Personal account of finishing a book through daily 30-45 minute sessions; motivating, but mostly anecdote rather than a transferable technique.

title: Opinion against smart home gadgets
why: Strong opinion that smart home devices add little and cause problems; anecdote-driven argument without technical explanation.

title: Why EV prices are the real adoption hurdle
why: Opinion on price barriers; cites battery cost but offers no rigorous analysis a reader could reuse.

title: Why Mastodon lacks mainstream appeal
why: Opinion about user adoption and product features; argues for consumer hooks, not technical insight.

title: Why big companies stay inefficient
why: Speculation about corporate equilibrium and inefficiency; open-ended questions rather than explanation.

title: Rebuttal to claims about cookware and TVs
why: Corrects several claims with opinion and light facts; argumentative, not a lesson a reader would bookmark.

title: Defense of Elastic against AWS
why: Argues AWS exploited open-source licensing; a business and ethics position rather than technical knowledge.

title: Musk, Kanye and free speech
why: Political commentary on speech platforms; opinion without substance.

title: Request for grocery delivery help
why: Personal help request during lockdown; no transferable lesson.

title: How HN flags and dupes actually behave
why: Moderator notes on flags and dupes; useful for HN readers but a moderation note, not technical learning.

title: Theory that peaceful societies self-destruct
why: Speculative sociological theory from travel and reading; opinion without evidence a reader can verify.

title: Wait before extracting repeated code
why: Let duplication survive a few changes first; either it stops looking repetitive, or a missed edit shows which parts truly need extraction.

title: Argument for class-based admissions
why: Personal account and policy opinion on affirmative action; not technical learning.

title: Measured Go vs Rust results on a text search
why: Both programs were naive, yet Rust finished in about 4.2s versus Go's 6.5s with less memory; measure before trusting language-speed claims.

title: A personal account of depression
why: Personal mental health story; not a technical lesson and best treated as personal content only.

title: Why roaming passkeys still carry phishing risk
why: Syncing passkeys to the cloud by design means attestation can't enforce device binding; they still beat passwords, but phishing resistance has limits.

title: Request for evidence on remote productivity
why: Asks for research on co-located teams; a plea and opinion rather than findings.

title: Decoding a dense k one-liner step by step
why: k has few syntax forms: applying functions, infix operators, bracket argument lists and adverbs; a short line decodes once these rules are known.

title: Practical ways to promote a new web app
why: Pitch smaller niche blogs with rapport, join competitor user communities, and seek interviews; small friendly blogs link more readily than big ones.

title: Replacing the README's examples with sed and find
why: Each README example maps to sed -r with find and xargs; standard Unix tools cover bulk edits, file filtering and previews.

title: Anecdote about buying durable blenders
why: Personal shopping story about planned obsolescence; buy-premium advice rests on a few products.

title: Argument about political engagement
why: Political opinion about Trump and voter representation; no technical learning.

title: Curated starting resources for learning Clojure
why: Concise wikibook intro, clojure.org rationale, Emacs setup guides and Rich Hickey videos; many tutorials assume a Java background.

title: Why Copilot can seem to emit private code
why: Context comes from open local files, and frequently repeated patterns get reproduced; the team says such repeats occur in under 1% of suggestions.

title: Personal list of climate actions
why: Personal list of lifestyle changes like flights, meat and phones; framed as action, with no new technical insight.

title: Grad school story about questionable data
why: Anecdote about questionable lab results and a colleague; a story with no transferable technique.

title: Why fusion's tritium problem isn't solved
why: Practical fusion plants need tritium breeding, and tritium is hard to contain, so fusion's stigma and proliferation issues aren't obviously smaller than fission's.

title: Income from indie macOS apps
why: Personal business report on app revenue in a niche; useful context but mostly a personal story, not a technique to learn.

title: How big-company software buying really works
why: Purchasing departments negotiate discounts by default, and 80-question checklists come from junior staff who hand evaluation to vendors who answer yes.

title: Argument that ad blocking drives native advertising
why: Opinion about ad blocking's moral effects and native advertising; argument rather than explanation.

title: Cartels and government power
why: Political commentary on cartels and legalization; opinion, not technical.

title: Career stress after becoming a manager
why: Personal career story about management and burnout; emotional and anecdotal without a transferable lesson.

title: Low-code tools for building a SaaS backend
why: Hasura autogenerates a GraphQL CRUD API from a database; pair it with Forest Admin, Metabase and PostHog for admin, BI and analytics.

title: Why a Brompton beats other folding bikes
why: Brompton rides like a real bike with gears and large-enough wheels; cheaper small-wheel folders compromise ride quality and gearing.

title: Critique of travel as consumerism
why: Opinion about travel versus local learning; rhetorical argument rather than evidence or practical technique.

title: Asking advice on an ICO
why: Founder asking for advice about a company's ICO plan; situational, with no general lesson.

title: Defense of front-end interview questions
why: Opinion on which interview questions are fair; argues for topics without new explanation.

title: Humans lack emotional object permanence
why: Opinion about social presence and promotions; a personal claim, not an explanation a reader could verify.

title: Motivational advice to find a customer
why: Motivational advice to build for a specific person; encouragement rather than technical learning.

title: Why web apps should save files to disk
why: Opinion that cloud apps should store data locally; argument about incentives rather than explanation.

title: Why decentralized networks drift toward centralization
why: Running a node costs time and money, and unequal spending lets a few providers dominate even under decentralized protocols, as GitHub does for Git.

title: What Google Cloud Messaging actually carries in Signal
why: Signal uses GCM only as a wake-up push on Android; no message data goes over it, and the app fetches messages from Signal's server.

title: Nostalgia for the iPod and album listening
why: Personal nostalgia about music listening and devices; no technical lesson.

title: Brendan Eich on Dart and web fragmentation
why: Standards politics about Dart and browser fragmentation; advocacy rather than a technical explanation.

title: Why Tesla Autopilot drove into a stationary barrier
why: Vision tracks lanes and car rears while radar ignores stationary objects, so a gore area that looks like a lane leads into the barrier.

title: Using reviews to decide whether to stay
why: Personal framework for judging managers and coworkers; advice, not a technical explanation.

title: Argument for fully managed serverless
why: Opinion that managed serverless avoids operations entirely; argumentative, with little concrete technical comparison.

title: Argument against crypto bans
why: Political and economic opinion about money and mining; argument rather than explanation.

title: Anecdote about discontinued favorite products
why: Humorous personal anecdote about products being discontinued; no technical lesson.

title: Critique of Steve Jobs' contributions
why: Opinion piece criticizing Jobs' technical credit; argument with few verifiable explanations.

title: Ask HN: what tech made worse
why: Personal opinions about ads, social media and durability; no concrete technical learning.

title: Comparing company PRISM denials
why: Observes near-identical company statements about PRISM; an observation about corporate language, not technical knowledge.

title: Why working from home won't stick
why: Personal and management opinion on remote work; reasons are plausible but not evidence-based.

title: Factual rebuttal of Bolt's HN claims
why: Dispute over HN ranking and timing; a moderator's rebuttal of one company's claims, not a technical lesson.

title: How intonation separates 'could care less' from literal use
why: Listeners tell idioms from literal phrases by intonation contour, as with 'black bird' stressed versus flat; the same words map to different referents.

title: Why pointers click when you picture memory
why: Pointers become clear when you picture raw memory and what's actually stored, instead of parsing the syntax, which confused the author for years.

title: Simple wardrobe rules for tech workers
why: Fit matters more than brand: fitted solid shirts, well-fitting jeans, and a tailored suit with two white shirts cover most situations.

title: Lessons from the Taos operating system startup
why: Tao's OS translated a custom portable assembly to native code at load; a proprietary language and hard-to-say name hurt adoption.

title: Learning from works versus copying them
why: Copyright protects expression, not learned concepts or facts, so training may be fair use; infringement arises mainly from reproducing enough verbatim text.

title: Burnout as a learned link between work and failure
why: Repeated high-risk failures condition the brain to associate work with failure; small guaranteed wins restore the reward signal and prevent burnout.

title: Build habits with the Tiny Habits recipe
why: Shrink the habit until it needs no willpower, anchor it to an existing routine, then celebrate right away; this worked where earlier attempts failed.

title: Source code and courses worth studying
why: Study xv6 and MIT 6.824 labs for OS and distributed systems, Tarsnap for C style, and Arc for implementing a Lisp.

title: Dynamic languages in large teams: a double-edged sword
why: Hyper-dynamic languages suit small projects and disciplined teams; with juniors and no architectural owner, flexibility creates staggering tech debt.

title: Advice to fix an Airbnb incident
why: Public demand for a company to make amends; advocacy and business advice rather than technical learning.

title: Frustration with the tech industry
why: Broad complaint about VC funding and over-engineering; opinion without a concrete, verifiable explanation.

title: Studies find no cognitive effect of CO2 at high levels
why: Military studies found no cognitive effects from CO2 up to 40,000 ppm; exhaled breath already reaches about that, so office levels are unlikely to matter.

title: Why renting hash power enables double-spend attacks
why: If hash power can be rented at market rates, a 51% attack earns fees and enables double-spends, so no fee level alone deters it.

title: Review of the Nexus 6 phone
why: Consumer product opinion on screen size, battery and price; no lasting technical lesson.

title: Android users and AirTag tracking
why: Opinion that AirTags should be discontinued; argument mainly about risk, with limited explanation of detection.

title: Deduplicating encrypted files via content-hash keys
why: Encrypt each file with a key derived from its own hash: identical files produce identical ciphertext, so the server deduplicates without seeing plaintext.

title: The campfire model of friendship
why: Personal reflection on giving to others and loneliness; philosophical, not technical.

title: Argument that inflation is not a threat
why: Economic opinion about money creation and CPI; argumentative rather than instructive.

title: Deliverability lessons for running a newsletter
why: Mail providers penalize non-openers and suspicious TLDs like .tk; tracking pixels help spot disengaged subscribers, and routing links through your own domain avoids blocks.

title: Commentary on 2004 tech predictions
why: Annotated retrospective of predictions; mostly opinion and hindsight, without a technical explanation.

title: Rant about noisy open offices
why: Personal complaint about office noise and hot-desking; no technical lesson.

title: Downsides of full pay transparency
why: Personal experience and opinion on compensation schemes; argues against transparency without verifiable evidence.

title: Why cities feel hostile to families
why: Social and urban opinion built on vivid description; argument rather than evidence or technique.

title: Wishlist for non-Apple premium laptops
why: Product wishlist and complaints about PC makers; opinion about hardware rather than explanation.

title: Argument to split Apple
why: Political and business opinion on App Store control; argument with no technical explanation.

title: Why Firefox couldn't evolve its old extension API
why: Breaking an internal API means porting code, shims, chasing add-on authors and maintaining both APIs for a year, which blocked optimizations like Quantum.
